title: ALP JSON-RPC v1 IPC
description: Messages of ALP JSON-RPC protocol v1 (docs/protocol/alp-json-rpc-v1.md). One JSON value per frame; unknown properties, event types and item kinds are accepted for forward compatibility.

oneOf.description: A terminal's output, exit or detach (capability terminal, §12.10).
The live model catalog changed (capability catalog.live): re-read catalog.get.

reload.description: Whether session.reload can restart this root's native process (§12.8); the root must also be open and idle.

configure.description: Whether session.configure can change this root's model, effort or team (§12.9); the root must also be open and idle.

projectRoot.description: An absolute, normalized path on the daemon host to a directory holding .alp/. Compared as is: the daemon never walks up to a parent.

secretMarker.description: Stands for a stored secret value: read results carry it in place of the value; a save that sends it back keeps the stored value.

attachment.description: A committed attachment as clients see it: ids, display metadata and its digest, never a host path or URL.

forkProvenance.description: Where a fork came from (§12.7): the source root, and the turn its conversation was cut at.

conversationBranch.description: Later turns a rewind set aside (§12.7): kept, never deleted, recoverable as a new session with session.fork { branchId }.

effectiveConfig.description: The configuration a root runs with, or would after a change, as alpd resolved it (§12.9).

permissionProfile.description: The permission profile capping the agent's mode, when one does.

delegates.description: Agents the root may delegate to.

tools.description: ALP tools the root's agent is given.

hooks.description: How many hook commands the agent runs.

restart.description: Whether applying it restarts the root's native process (on its own conversation).

allowed.description: Whether session.configure would take it now; a busy tree may still refuse it later.

terminal.description: A terminal as clients see it: ids, size and state, never a process id, shell path or host path.

protection.description: Absent: full native process protection (macOS, supported Linux). root-only: best-effort Linux; closing ends the shell, but processes it started may keep running. none: Windows platform PTY (ConPTY); cleanup is best-effort and not guaranteed. Clients show a non-blocking notice.

terminalEvent.description: params of a terminal.event notification (§12.10): sent only to the connection attached to the terminal.
